# Canadian Renewable Energy Dataset Inventory

This interactive web map brings together a comprehensive suite of renewable energy datasets created by CanmetENERGY-Ottawa to support renewable energy knowledge, planning, and research across Canada. The combined layers include the locations of current Canadian wind energy projects, offshore wind suitability in Atlantic Canada, hydrokinetic river resources, low-head hydropower opportunities, solar irradiance potential, and standardized weather datasets for energy modelling. Together, these datasets provide an overview of Canada’s renewable energy landscape spanning different technology areas, including wind, solar, and marine energy, while integrating existing infrastructure and future development potential. This platform enables users to compare spatial patterns, assess resource availability, and support evidence-based decision-making for clean energy planning, research, and policy development.

## Canadian Wind Turbine Database

This dataset provides the locations and technical specifications of wind turbines across Canada, including capacity, rotor diameter, hub height, and commissioning date. It supports analysis of installed wind energy capacity, spatial distribution, and project development trends. The layer is intended to be used for energy planning, grid integration studies, and environmental assessments.

The Canadian Wind Turbine Database is also accessible at: https://app.geo.ca/en-ca/map-browser/record/79fdad93-9025-49ad-ba16-c26d718cc070

## Preliminary Considerations Analysis of Offshore Wind Energy in Atlantic Canada

This dataset supports early-stage planning and strategic assessment of offshore renewable energy opportunities in Atlantic Canada and features key physical, human, and environmental considerations and constraints for offshore wind development, including wind resource potential, ecologically sensitive areas, existing ocean energy uses, and physical constraints. These layers, containing the various physical, human, and environmental considerations that define suitability, are accessible at: https://app.geo.ca/en-ca/map-browser/record/29fd13f3-e7d5-4291-8560-69d405a64a3f

## Hydrokinetic Resource Mapping – Optical Satellite Imagery Analysis of Open Water Regions in Ice-Covered Canadian Rivers

This dataset maps open water regions in ice-covered rivers using satellite imagery to assess hydrokinetic energy potential. It identifies areas where flowing water remains accessible during winter conditions, which is critical for year-round energy generation. The layer supports feasibility studies for in-stream turbine deployment and cold-climate renewable energy research.

The complete dataset of open water regions in ice-covered Canadian rivers is accessible at: https://app.geo.ca/en-ca/map-browser/record/61b4e576-9f3a-49a1-9546-b29be14787a4

## Canadian Weather Year for Energy Calculation (CWEC)

CWEC provides typical meteorological year data derived from historical weather observations for building energy simulations and renewable energy modelling. The dataset includes hourly values for variables such as temperature, wind speed, solar radiation, and humidity. It is widely used for heating, cooling, and renewable energy performance analysis.

This layer indicates the 644 locations for which detailed data is available. The entire CWEC database can be accessed at: https://app.geo.ca/en-ca/map-browser/record/55438acb-aa67-407a-9fdb-1cb21eb24e28

## Canadian Weather Energy and Engineering Datasets (CWEEDS)

CWEEDS offers long-term historical hourly weather data from climate stations across the country. The dataset supports engineering design, energy modelling, and risk assessment by providing detailed climate variables over extended time periods. It is particularly valuable for infrastructure planning and renewable resource assessment.

This map indicates the 644 locations for which detailed data is available. The entire CWEEDS database can be accessed at: https://app.geo.ca/en-ca/map-browser/record/005494f2-1848-48d5-abe4-a76a7846f035

## Daily Average Solar Irradiance on Tilted Surfaces for All of Canada

This dataset provides modelled averaged daily solar radiation values for all of Canada for 10 different tilt angles from the time period 1998-2022. It enables comparison of solar energy potential across panel orientations and geographic locations. The dataset supports solar project siting, performance estimation, and regional renewable energy planning.

The layer displayed on this map represents daily average solar irradiance on a surface with two-axis tracking, which follows the sun throughout the day. Solar irradiance values for various tilted surfaces, including the one shown here, can be accessed at: https://app.geo.ca/en-ca/map-browser/record/1ab9f334-1e24-468b-bdc5-c086b3c19c8a

## Canada’s Low-Head Hydropower Resource Database: Sites with Head Under 15 m and Capacity Below 50 MW

This dataset identifies and characterizes potential low-head hydropower sites, including estimated capacity, head, and geographic location. It focuses on smaller-scale opportunities suitable for community, municipal, or distributed generation projects. The layer supports the evaluation of undeveloped hydropower resources and the expansion of clean energy.

The Low-Head Hydropower Resource Database can also be accessed at: https://app.geo.ca/en-ca/map-browser/record/1f961450-eab8-4bb3-abde-6c1554efbaed
